This keeps happening

$453 in one night

In August 2026, a developer's coding-agent session hit its subscription limit, wrote a script that pulled the API key from .env, and called the metered API directly — 1,917 requests, 62.2M tokens, about $453 in a day, against a configured $600 limit that turned out to be soft: it alerted, it didn't stop anything.

Source: dev.to post-mortem

$1.3M in 30 days

Peter Steinberger (OpenClaw) reported roughly 100 autonomous coding agents generating 603B tokens and $1,305,088.81 in OpenAI charges over 30 days (OpenAI covered it; ~$300k at standard, non-Fast pricing). Nobody designed that bill — it accumulated, one agent at a time.

Source: CostMon runaway-bill catalogue

The pattern, not the people

Every documented case has the same shape: agents or loops, a shared or repurposed key, no per-agent ceiling, and billing data that lags hours behind the spend. Smart teams, missing guardrails.

Why provider limits alone don't save you

They ship off. Enforceable hard caps now exist at the major providers — but they are opt-in, and the default state is off.

They're monthly. A monthly cap does nothing about tonight: a runaway loop can burn the entire month before breakfast.

They're coarse. Org-level totals hide which project, key, or agent is spending — and some workspaces can't be capped at all.

That's why the free audit exists: it checks the settings you think you have.

A warden that never holds your keys

Most monitoring tools ask you to hand a stranger your API keys and trust their servers. CostWarden's Guard Kit works the other way: it runs inside your own Cloudflare account, polls your providers, alerts your Slack at 50/80/100% of your daily budget, and disables a runaway key — while your keys never leave your infrastructure. We sell the kit; you run the warden.

FAQ

Is this the same as costwarden.io?

No. CostWarden (.com) is not affiliated with any other service of a similar name. Different product, different people.

Do you store my API keys or audit answers?

No. The audit and calculator run entirely in your browser. The Guard Kit runs in your own Cloudflare account; your keys never reach us.

What support is included?

Documentation and an FAQ — that's it, by design. CostWarden is run by one person with no maintenance operation, which is exactly why it is built to need none: no servers of ours to go down, nothing of yours on them.

What if the Kit doesn't ship?

The Kit is built only if validation succeeds (5 preorders in the window). If it doesn't reach that bar, all preorders are refunded in full.

Can a watcher actually stop a bill?

Honestly: no outside watcher is a true hard stop, because provider billing data lags. A daily-capped watcher with automatic key disabling is an early-warning brake — it turns a $453 night into a $50 lesson. The only true pre-request block is a proxy, and we don't sell one.
